narrativeReportMd:
# ProductShelfLife R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
ProductShelfLife has material local breaking changes. R4 instances that use the removed `identifier` element or the old mandatory `period` Quantity element are not valid against the R6 shape without transformation. R6 instances can also omit formerly mandatory data or use `periodString`, which is not cleanly representable in R4.

## Scope
The analysis covered the R4 and R6 ProductShelfLife core StructureDefinitions and supporting package metadata/indexes. Base artifact changes in Element/DataType/BackboneElement/BackboneType are out of scope, even though ProductShelfLife now derives from `BackboneType` rather than `BackboneElement`.

## Main migration themes
The datatype was simplified from the R4 local element set `identifier`, `type`, `period`, and `specialPrecautionsForStorage` to the R6 local element set `type`, `period[x]`, and `specialPrecautionsForStorage`. The highest-impact issue is the `period` reshape: it is no longer the JSON/XML element `period` of type Quantity, but a choice that serializes as `periodDuration` or `periodString` and is optional. `type` also changed from required to optional.

## Highest-impact findings
The main R4-to-R6 validation breaks are `ProductShelfLife.identifier` removal and replacement of mandatory `ProductShelfLife.period` Quantity with optional `ProductShelfLife.period[x]`. The main R6-to-R4 risk is that R6 can omit `type` and `period[x]`, and can use `periodString`, none of which can be represented as a valid R4 ProductShelfLife without policy-specific backfill or extensions.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for preserving any business identifiers that were stored in `identifier`, and for deciding how free-text or omitted R6 period values should be handled when producing R4-compatible data.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could likely have been staged less disruptively by retaining deprecated optional elements or by adding new optional text/choice-like elements instead of replacing existing element names. The local computable definitions do not include the rationale, so justification confidence is limited.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should own the base hierarchy shift and any inherited changes in `BackboneType`, `DataType`, `Element`, `Quantity`, and `Duration`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ProductShelfLife has local breaking changes: `identifier` was removed, mandatory `period` Quantity became optional `period[x]` with Duration/string wire names, and mandatory `type` became optional. The biggest uncertainty is the absence of official rationale or narrative diff explaining intended migration.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat ProductShelfLife as a reshaped datatype, not just a looser version of the R4 type. R4 `period` must be rewritten to `periodDuration` when it truly represents a duration, or reviewed/manual-mapped when it is a generic Quantity. R4 `identifier` requires a preservation decision because there is no R6 local replacement. R6-to-R4 conversion needs backfill policy for missing `type`/`period[x]` and a lossy strategy for `periodString`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both primary StructureDefinitions are present and the package indexes confirm the same canonical artifact exists in R6. Confidence is lower for intent and prevalence because official diffs, narrative ballot notes, and representative instance corpora were not supplied.

findings.title: ProductShelfLife.identifier was removed

oldState.summary: Optional local Identifier element was present.

semanticText.short: Unique identifier for the packaged Medicinal Product
semanticText.definition: Unique identifier for the packaged Medicinal Product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed one `ProductShelfLife.identifier` value of type `Identifier` and included it in summary content.

newState.summary: No corresponding local element exists in the R6 ProductShelfLife snapshot or differential.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 local element list contains `type`, `period[x]`, and `specialPrecautionsForStorage`; `identifier` is absent.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Matching is by exact ElementDefinition id/path. No R6 element has the same path or an obvious replacement with Identifier type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break for any R4 ProductShelfLife instance fragment containing `identifier`: the element is no longer part of the R6 content model. Strict validators reject unknown elements, generated R6 classes will not expose a local `identifier` property, and naive R4-to-R6 transforms will silently lose a business identifier if they only copy recognized R6 fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The element's R4 definition describes a unique identifier for the packaged medicinal product. Losing it can affect reconciliation, traceability, deduplication, or regulatory packaging workflows when systems used this local identifier.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove an identifier that may have belonged on the containing packaged product rather than the shelf-life component.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `identifier` as an optional deprecated base element while directing new R6 use to the appropriate containing product/package identifier.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing a semantically misplaced shelf-life identifier is a reasonable cleanup goal, but the break was probably avoidable at the base-design level. Because `identifier` was already optional and no R6 replacement exists inside ProductShelfLife, leaving it as deprecated 0..1 content would have preserved R4-valid instances and avoided unknown-element/data-loss failures while still signaling that new implementations should not populate it.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would keep `ProductShelfLife.identifier` as `0..1 Identifier`, mark it deprecated or retained only for cross-version compatibility, and clarify that identifiers normally belong on the containing packaged product or package resource. That is different from relying on conversion tooling or a backport extension: the R6 base content model itself would still accept old instances. The tradeoff is carrying a legacy element that may reflect poor modeling and may continue to be populated, but that cost appears manageable compared with dropping populated business identifiers.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with moderate legacy-modeling cost; the misplaced or duplicate identifier surface could persist but would not require a new same-datatype representation.

evidence.detail: R4 defines ProductShelfLife.identifier as 0..1 Identifier and summary=true.
R6 ProductShelfLife has no element with id or path ProductShelfLife.identifier.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative datatype fragments, not complete containing resources. The migration example uses a placeholder extension URL because the local R6 StructureDefinition does not provide an official replacement.

findings.narrativeMd: `ProductShelfLife.identifier` was a local R4 element and is absent from R6. This is more than a code-generation rename: R6 has no local Identifier-valued replacement, so systems that stored shelf-life or packaged-product identifiers here must decide where to preserve that data. The break is likely to be discovered as unknown-element validation errors, missing generated properties, or data loss during transformation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 fragment containing `identifier` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6 because R6 ProductShelfLife does not define that element. R6-to-R4 representability is not a problem for this specific removal because R6 has no corresponding data to carry back, but preservation of old R4 data requires an out-of-band mapping.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 data for populated `ProductShelfLife.identifier`. If it duplicates an identifier on the containing product/package resource, migrate it there with deduplication rules. If it has distinct meaning, preserve it with a governed extension and document the mapping. Tests should include populated and absent identifier cases and verify that transforms do not silently drop populated identifiers.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal may be justified if the identifier was semantically misplaced. A backward-compatible alternative would have been retaining an optional deprecated element or publishing a standard extension and mapping. That alternative would reduce data-loss risk but prolong support for a questionable modeling location.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended if real-world R4 instances populate this element, because the correct destination cannot be inferred from the ProductShelfLife StructureDefinition alone.

findings.title: Mandatory Quantity period was replaced by optional period[x] Duration|string

oldState.summary: R4 required a single Quantity-valued `period` element.

semanticText.short: The shelf life time period can be specified using a numerical value for the period of time and its unit of time measurement The unit of measurement shall be specified in accordance with ISO 11240 and the resulting terminology The symbol and the symbol identifier shall be used
semanticText.definition: The shelf life time period can be specified using a numerical value for the period of time and its unit of time measurement The unit of measurement shall be specified in accordance with ISO 11240 and the resulting terminology The symbol and the symbol identifier shall be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances used the property `period` with a Quantity object, and the element was mandatory.

newState.summary: R6 defines optional choice element `period[x]` with allowed types Duration and string.

semanticText.short: The shelf life time period can be specified using a numerical value for the period of time and its unit of time measurement The unit of measurement shall be specified in accordance with ISO 11240 and the resulting terminology The symbol and the symbol identifier shall be used
semanticText.definition: The shelf life time period can be specified using a numerical value for the period of time and its unit of time measurement The unit of measurement shall be specified in accordance with ISO 11240 and the resulting terminology The symbol and the symbol identifier shall be used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 instances use choice serialization such as `periodDuration` or `periodString`; `period` is no longer the wire element name.

facts.note: A non-choice element became a choice element.
FHIR choice elements serialize with type suffixes.

facts.oldValue: R4 ProductShelfLife.period used Quantity without a local ProductShelfLife-specific time-unit invariant.
facts.newValue: R6 periodDuration uses Duration, whose datatype requires time-unit semantics when code is present.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element has the same business description and parent and keeps the base name `period`, but R6 makes it a FHIR choice element. This is a high-confidence replacement rather than a separate unrelated addition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This change breaks both validation and generated APIs. An R4 instance with `period` is not using a valid R6 choice wire name, and R6 generated models will expose a polymorphic `period[x]`/`periodDuration`/`periodString` pattern rather than a required Quantity property. Conversely, R6 can omit the period or represent it as free text, neither of which can be rendered as a required R4 Quantity without loss or policy-specific inference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Shelf-life period is core business/regulatory data for product storage and expiry handling. Incorrect or lost mapping can affect product usability, labeling, inventory, or compliance decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow shelf-life periods to be represented either as formal durations or as free text, and no longer require a period in every instance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep legacy `period` as optional Quantity and add a separate optional text element for non-computable shelf-life statements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears reasonable: represent computable shelf-life intervals with a time-specific datatype, permit narrative shelf-life statements, and allow contexts where no period is known. A less-breaking design could cover many R4 instances, but it would not achieve the same clean single-choice model and would retain a broad legacy Quantity path for regulatory shelf-life duration data. Given those material tradeoffs, the breaking choice conversion is probably justified, though the absence of official rationale prevents a stronger verdict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would change the old `period` element to `0..1 Quantity` while adding something like `periodText` for free-text cases and, if needed, an invariant or guidance to avoid populating both. This would preserve R4 wire names for existing Quantity periods and support the common narrative-use goal. It is only partial because the model would have two same-resource ways to state the shelf-life period, validators and implementers would need rules for conflicts or precedence, and the old Quantity element would keep accepting content less specific than Duration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 data but creates parallel same-fact representations, ambiguity when both are populated, and continued acceptance of broad Quantity content instead of a cleaner Duration|string choice.

evidence.detail: R4 defines ProductShelfLife.period as min=1 max=1 type=Quantity.
R6 defines ProductShelfLife.period[x] as min=0 max=1 with types Duration and string.
Duration carries a time-unit constraint when code is present, making it semantically narrower than a generic Quantity.
evidence.quote: There SHALL be a code if there is a value and it SHALL be an expression of time. If system is present, it SHALL be UCUM.

r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.periodString: until the printed expiry date after reconstitution

examples.examplesMd: The old-to-new example is a straightforward Quantity-to-Duration rewrite for a computable time unit. It is not a universal lossless transform: arbitrary R4 Quantity content or R6 `periodString` content needs manual or policy-specific handling.

findings.narrativeMd: `ProductShelfLife.period` changed from a required Quantity element to an optional FHIR choice element. This simultaneously changes the wire name, generated code shape, cardinality, and allowable value domain. Even when an R4 Quantity is semantically a duration and can be copied into a Duration-shaped object, the serialized property changes from `period` to `periodDuration`; systems that only rename classes or copy fields will fail validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid data with `period` can be R6-invalid because `period` is no longer a valid R6 choice serialization. R6-valid data can be not R4-representable when `period[x]` is absent or when the value is `periodString`. Generated code must also change from a required Quantity property to an optional polymorphic choice, affecting null checks, type switches, FHIRPath paths, JSON/XML serializers, and schema validation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, transform `period` to `periodDuration` only when the Quantity genuinely represents a duration; validate UCUM/time-unit assumptions. For ambiguous or non-time quantities, route to manual review or a governed extension rather than coercing silently. For R6-to-R4, define policy for missing `period[x]` and `periodString`, such as rejecting, backfilling from context, using an extension plus placeholder Quantity where allowed by local policy, or accepting lossy conversion. Test all choice arms and missing-period cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 choice is semantically expressive but was not backward-compatible at the wire level. Retaining a deprecated `period` element, adding a separate text element, or relaxing requiredness through profiles would have reduced breakage while addressing many expressivity goals. The tradeoff is that those alternatives are less clean than a single polymorphic choice and may preserve an overly broad Quantity type.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding combines element identity, cardinality, type-domain, and serialization effects because they are inseparable for a FHIR choice conversion.

findings.title: ProductShelfLife.type minimum cardinality decreased from 1 to 0

oldState.summary: R4 required exactly one CodeableConcept type.

semanticText.short: This describes the shelf life, taking into account various scenarios such as shelf life of the packaged Medicinal Product itself, shelf life after transformation where necessary and shelf life after the first opening of a bottle, etc. The shelf life type shall be specified using an appropriate controlled vocabulary The controlled term and the controlled term identifier shall be specified
semanticText.definition: This describes the shelf life, taking into account various scenarios such as shelf life of the packaged Medicinal Product itself, shelf life after transformation where necessary and shelf life after the first opening of a bottle, etc. The shelf life type shall be specified using an appropriate controlled vocabulary The controlled term and the controlled term identifier shall be specified.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every R4 ProductShelfLife was required to classify the kind of shelf life being described.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same CodeableConcept element but makes it optional.

semanticText.short: This describes the shelf life, taking into account various scenarios such as shelf life of the packaged Medicinal Product itself, shelf life after transformation where necessary and shelf life after the first opening of a bottle, etc. The shelf life type shall be specified using an appropriate controlled vocabulary The controlled term and the controlled term identifier shall be specified
semanticText.definition: This describes the shelf life, taking into account various scenarios such as shelf life of the packaged Medicinal Product itself, shelf life after transformation where necessary and shelf life after the first opening of a bottle, etc. The shelf life type shall be specified using an appropriate controlled vocabulary The controlled term and the controlled term identifier shall be specified.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits ProductShelfLife without a type classification.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element has the same id, path, type, definition, and summary flag in both versions; only the minimum cardinality changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because every R4 instance that satisfied `type` still satisfies the R6 cardinality. It is still a migration and runtime risk because R6 data can omit a field that R4 required, and generated R6 models must treat `type` as nullable/optional where R4 code may have assumed it was always present.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The type distinguishes scenarios such as unopened product shelf life, post-transformation shelf life, or after first opening. Omitting it can make downstream shelf-life interpretation ambiguous.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow ProductShelfLife entries where the shelf-life category is unknown, implicit, or not required by the containing context.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 preservation because decreasing the minimum cardinality from 1 to 0 does not invalidate R4 instances that already contain `type`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. R4-valid ProductShelfLife instances that contain the required `type` remain valid with respect to this element in R6, so there is no less-breaking R6 base design needed to preserve R4 instances. The relaxation likely improves implementability for contexts where the shelf-life category is unknown or implied, while the real cost is weaker semantic guarantees for R6 consumers and R6-to-R4 conversion.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the base R6 change is a relaxation, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` should be `Not applicable` under the calibration rules. Systems needing the R4 guarantee can use R6 profiles, invariants, or exchange rules that require `type`, but those are conformance choices for stricter contexts rather than backward-compatible alternatives to a breaking R4-to-R6 base change.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining concern is reverse conversion and consumer null-handling; stricter profiles can require `type` where cross-version exchange or business rules need it.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment illustrates omission of `type`. Any R4-compatible conversion would need a real CodeableConcept or an agreed placeholder; placeholder text can be semantically lossy.

findings.narrativeMd: `ProductShelfLife.type` remains the same CodeableConcept element, but R6 no longer requires it. This weakens validation rather than breaking old R4 instances, but it is material for systems that convert R6 back to R4 or whose business rules assume every shelf-life entry says what kind of shelf life is being described.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances remain valid with respect to this element in R6. R6-valid instances that omit `type` cannot be valid R4 ProductShelfLife without adding a CodeableConcept. Generated clients, validators, and business logic must treat `type` as optional in R6 and should not dereference it unconditionally.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, no transform is required beyond accepting that the field is now optional. For R6-to-R4, define a backfill rule from context where possible; otherwise reject, flag for review, or use an agreed placeholder only if downstream consumers understand it. Add tests for missing `type` because R4-era code may not handle null.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because this is a relaxation, it is not a hard R4-to-R6 break. The backward-compatibility concern is primarily reverse conversion and consumer assumptions. A profile-level relaxation or best-practice warning could have preserved the base guarantee while allowing specific contexts to omit the type.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 counterpart has the same canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, derivation, and abstract=false. The baseDefinition and maturity/status changed, but the base hierarchy shift is out of scope and the status change is noted as non-breaking.

No ProductShelfLife-owned element declares a local terminology binding in either version. The CodeableConcept elements remain locally unbound; Duration's datatype-level binding is a dependency consideration rather than a ProductShelfLife binding change.
ProductShelfLife has no Reference-typed local elements in either R4 or R6.

No ProductShelfLife-specific invariant was added or removed on local business elements. The common `ele-1` constraint remains. Inherited extension/base constraint differences are explicitly out of scope.
No local business element is a modifier in either version. `modifierExtension` remains inherited modifier content and is out of scope as a base-artifact concern.
No local ProductShelfLife business element has slicing in either version. Extension slicing is inherited/base behavior.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value appears on ProductShelfLife-owned business elements in either version.
No ProductShelfLife-owned business element has minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limits in either version.

Definitions for surviving business concepts `type`, `period`, and `specialPrecautionsForStorage` are materially unchanged. Structural changes to `period` and cardinality changes to `type` carry the material impact rather than narrative text changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The status and standards-status metadata do not change the instance wire format or validation content model by themselves.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and implementation planning should notice that R6 treats ProductShelfLife as more mature, even though the local shape also changed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added root mapping `administrative.medication` is metadata for classification/mapping and does not make any instance invalid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that consumes mappings may categorize ProductShelfLife differently in R6, but ordinary instance validation is unaffected.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: specialPrecautionsForStorage remains stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `specialPrecautionsForStorage` keeps the same path, cardinality `0..*`, CodeableConcept type, summary flag, and definition.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Existing mappings for this element should carry forward directly, subject only to any out-of-scope CodeableConcept/base datatype changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: ProductShelfLife's R6 baseDefinition is `BackboneType` rather than R4 `BackboneElement`. Per scope rules this global base hierarchy issue belongs to base-artifact reports, not this local ProductShelfLife report.
The new `periodDuration` choice arm relies on Duration datatype semantics, constraints, and terminology. Duration-level breaking changes should be assessed in the Duration report.
R4 `period` used Quantity, while R6 periodDuration uses Duration derived from Quantity. Quantity-level changes are dependencies but not local ProductShelfLife findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change note, or Jira rationale was available. Structural confidence is high, but justification and intended migration path confidence are lower.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official HL7 diff pages, Jira tickets, or committee notes for ProductShelfLife.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No representative R4/R6 instance corpus was analyzed, so prevalence of populated `identifier`, non-time Quantity `period`, missing R6 `type`, or `periodString` use is unknown.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run the comparison against production or published example instances containing ProductShelfLife.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions were not compared. This has limited effect on local ProductShelfLife findings because the datatype itself declares no local bindings, but it could refine assessment of Duration-related unit constraints.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare R4/R6 expansions for Duration units and related Quantity value sets if detailed period-unit compatibility is required.
